books.title: Project Rose #1
books.synopsis: Benedict Springwood witnessed a murder! But no one believes him. He reaches out to a skilled detective, Lady Holmes. The duo work together to solve the case, only to realise they got themselves into a bigger problem!

books.title: Book Two: Petals of the Underground
books.synopsis: With the truth about her bloodline exposed, Rose has to choose between the badge she swore to and the family she never asked for — while a new power stirs beneath Foraville's streets.

books.title: Book Three: What the Roses Remember
books.synopsis: The final bloom. Old allies, old enemies, and a city that has to decide what kind of story it wants to tell about itself.

1.title: Chapter 1: Lady Holmes
content: Sunflower District 221b.
A man studied the address written on the piece of paper he was holding. Apparently, a woman with detective skills so exceptional that people call her "Lady Holmes".

He went up a flight of stairs between a cafe and a flower shop. The place felt hidden; it would be hard to find if someone did not pay attention. Potted plants were everywhere, lining the stairs, hanging from hooks, even clustered around the entrance, almost swallowing the doorway whole.
As he reached the end of the stairs, he saw a door. There was a sign dangling. ROSE DETECTIVE AGENCY.
What an interesting name, the man thought to himself.
He pressed the doorbell, waiting for a response. No one answered.
Is no one home? He thought.
He leaned in and tried pressing the doorbell again. This time, he heard rushing footsteps coming from the inside.
It must be her! His heart was beating with anticipation.
Suddenly, the door swung open violently, hitting him in the face. Pain shot up his nose and he stumbled backwards, landing on the floor behind him.
"Why does the door open outward?!" he yelled while rubbing his painful nose.
"Oh no! I'm so sorry!" said a woman's voice.
He lifted his head, wincing at the sharp throb in his nose.

Standing in the doorway was a young woman, probably in her twenties, wearing a dress with a pleated skirt layered with brown and cream tones, completed with a brown plaid capelet and a matching beret tilted on her head. Her long pink hair was tied into neat twintails with ribbons. Her eyes are pink, like rose-tinted glass.
"Are you OK, sir?!" she asked, clearly distressed.
"Don't worry, I'm fine." The man stood up and tidied his white dyed hair. He brushed off the dust on his black coat and addressed his question, "Might you be Lady Holmes?"
"Eh, oh...yes...how did you get here?" She paused and hesitated before answering.
"I followed the address on this paper...it was left on my desk..." He passed the paper to her.
She skimmed through the paper and let out a sigh of relief. "Haha, I see! So what can I do for you?"
"I have a case for you," The man said in a serious voice.
"I see. Please come in," she responded.

The agency had a charming vintage aesthetic. Warm light shone gently across the room, reflecting off polished wood and glass. The tall bookshelves are filled with books and files. There are two couches facing each other in the middle of the room. Fresh roses are placed in a vase on the table. As the man took a seat, he could smell the faint fragrance of the roses that quietly filled the room.
The man noticed a photo placed on the wall. It was a photo of a family.
She has a nice family, he guessed.
"So, what is the case about?" she asked. The man diverted his attention back to Lady Holmes.
"I......Witnessed a murder."
Lady Holmes' face was filled with shock. "What?! Shouldn't you call the police first?!"
"I did!" he cried. "But no one believed me."
"What do you mean?" She asked in disbelief.
"I was a cop." he explained, "2 days ago, in the evening around 5.30 pm, when I was patrolling in an alley, I saw a hooded person kill a woman by strangling."
"I tried to catch the person, but I lost them." he lowered my head in guilt. "I tried to call back up. When they arrived, I guided them to the body, but when we reached there, the body disappeared!"
"Could it be an invisibility power user?" Lady Holmes reasoned calmly.
"No, I don't think so." the man objected.
"Why?"
"Because I have a power-sensing ability."
Lady Holmes gave him a look of doubt.
"When I look at someone for 3 seconds, the details of their power will be revealed to me," he clarified.
"Really?" Lady Holmes doesn't seem to believe him.
"Yes," the man said firmly.
He looked at her for 3 seconds; every detail of her power projected in front of his eyes, like a virtual overlay only he could see.
"Your power is power mimicry, isn't it?"
"......yes," Lady Holmes mumbled.
"Then copy my power. Then you'll know I'm telling the truth." The man suggested, wanting her to trust him.
"Alright." She seems convinced.
Lady Holmes walked up to him. She placed her hand on his shoulder. Her rose-tinted eyes start to glow like two sparkling diamonds.
The glow faded, and she looked into his eyes.
The details of the man's power are shown to her. She nodded and said, "It is true."

Lady Holmes read through the details. "Power sensing. When looking at a target for 3 seconds, the details of their power will be revealed. Only effective on living things. Side effect: a headache if used too much."

"No one believed me, since my power wasn't obvious." The man sighed. "I tried my power on the killer, but I couldn't sense anything. That means they're just normal human. How did they make the body disappear within such a short time?"
Lady Holmes pondered. She remained silent for a while and gave him a grin. "This case is interesting. I'll take on your case!"
"Thank you so much! Lady Holmes!" the man cheered.
"Of course!" she giggled. "You can just call me Alice. Pleased to make your acquaintance."
"I'm Benedict Springwood. Same to you."

2.title: Chapter 2: I'm not going back there!
content: "Alright! Let's go through all the details" Alice said as she stood up, grabbing a marker. She walked to the whiteboard behind the couch and began writing.

1. A WOMAN WAS KILLED BY A HOODED PERSON IN AN ALLEY
2. THE PERSON IS NOT A POWER USER
3. THE CORPSE DISAPPEARED WHEN MR. SPRINGWOOD IS AWAY. IT WAS LESS THAN A MINUTE
"Ok! First of all, we need to find out who the woman is. That way, it's easier to identify suspects!" said Alice.
"How do we do that?" Benedict asked.
"We can look through the power user records!" Alice suggested. "More than half of Foraville's citizens are power users. She might be one too! We can start from there."
"Wait! The power user records?!" Benedict yelled in fear, and cold sweat rolled down his face; his legs started to shake.
"That's right! We are going to the Foraville Police Headquarters!" she announced loudly.
"No! No! No!" Benedict protested.
"Why?" Alice asked.

"I was kicked out of there like just yesterday?! For y'know, causing a ruckus because of the murder?! And you want me to go back?!" He was strongly against the idea of going back there. It's so embarrassing! He panicked.

Ever since seeing the corpse disappear, he tried so hard to convince them that it was real. However, the force just thought he was hallucinating. He put so much effort into explaining it, even sending a letter to the higher-ups, hoping they would start investigating it. But it was useless. They got annoyed at him for causing this whole mess, and he got put on indefinite leave.
I didn't want to give up. He thought. And just before leaving the station, he noticed a piece of paper on his desk, with an address scribbled on it, with a short note saying "Lady Holmes might help".
And here he is, pleading with her not to go back there.
"Please don't let me go back there", Benedict kneeled on the floor with his hands clasped together. "I can already imagine their fierce stares that could pierce a hole in my soul!"
"Oh, c'mon, you're exaggerating!" Alice rolled her eyes. "I know most of the police officers there. I can cover for you!" She grabs his arm and pulls him up.
"I have a bad feeling about this..." The unsettling feeling in him continues.

They departed from the agency. As they exited the stairs, the warmth of the afternoon sun was felt. The sky above was clear and blue. A gentle breeze carried the scent of flowers through the air. The streets are filled with pedestrians, bustling with life. The smell of flowers filled the air, butterflies fluttered around the flowers gracefully.

The weather in Foraville shifts depending on the district. Sunflower District is in the centre of Foraville. It's not too hot here; temperatures are just right. However, the temperature falls much lower once it rains. The area in the East, Periwinkle's farm is sunny and humid all year long, perfect for farming. The North, where lotus dock was situated, experiences summer the whole year, thus the beach is a great tourist spot. The weather in the South and West, ranging from bluebell to lavender district is chilly. Snow falls at the end of every year.

Benedict glanced at Alice, who is walking beside him. She walks in a cheerful manner, and she hums a melody while walking down the streets, as if they weren't heading straight to a place full of people who might throw him out all over again.
"Miss Alice." He called out to her, seemingly curious about something.
"Yes?" She turned her head and looked at him.
"The officers at the station said you're famous, but I never saw you in the newspapers before."
"Oh, that's because my family forbade me from appearing in newspapers. They're just worried about my safety, since being a detective is a risky job. Vengeful people might come looking for me."
"True." He agreed with her reason.
"That's why you can only contact me through the police!" She clarified. "All clients' requests are sent to the police station to be delivered to me."
"Wow, how secretive." Benedict was impressed by all the effort.
As they were chatting, they reached the police headquarters building.
"We're here!" cheered Alice. "Let's go!" She turned around to realise Benedict had disappeared.
He was hiding behind a tree, and fear had gotten to him.
There is no way I'm setting foot in that building ever again. He yelled internally.
Alice ran to him and grabbed his arm. "Let's go! Stop worrying!"
"No!!!" Benedict exerted all his strength hugging the tree but Alice managed to pull him away from it.
"How are you so strong?!" He yelled in disbelief.
She continues dragging him towards the entrance. There is no escaping this fate.
"Hey guys!!" greeted Alice cheerfully as she pushed the door open.
Police officers were everywhere; they all lifted their heads. "Lady Holmes!" They all greeted her back in a cheerful manner.
Suddenly, their eyes shifted to Benedict standing behind Alice. Their gazes changed from a friendly tone to a serious one.
I want to get out of here! He cried internally.
"Pierce!" Alice called out to the officer at the counter.
"Oh, Rosebloom," said the officer.
Rosebloom? Benedict thought as he overheard the officer call out to Alice. He felt a sense of familiarity in that name, but he couldn't remember what and brushed it off.

The officer turned to Alice as she walked towards him. He was Benedict's former superior when he was still on the force. He's tall, with pale skin that made his dark circles stand out even more. He had slightly messy charcoal grey hair like he hadn't had time to fix it.
His dark red eyes shifted to Benedict with a stern glare as he noticed his presence.
"Hello, Detective Doberman..." Benedict greeted him nervously. He lowered my head, afraid to meet his scary gaze.
"Springwood," Pierce replied with an unfriendly tone.
"So, how's it going?" Pierce asked Alice.
"We're investigating the murder!" informed Alice. "Can we check out the power user records, please? We might have a clue on who's the victim!" She leaned towards Pierce and lowered her voice.
"Oh my days, why are you brainwashed by him too?!" growled Pierce. "We already investigated, there's no one in that area that has the power to make a corpse disappear!"
"Well...There's you." Alice pointed at Pierce.
Benedict turned and looked at Pierce for information. His power is invisibility. He can turn invisible and make anything else disappear as long as he is in contact with it as long as he's focused.

"I have an alibi, I was at the station. You can check the CCTV footage if you're onto me." Pierce rolled his eyes. "Besides, don't you think Springwood might be hallucinating? Maybe he didn't get enough sleep the night before."

"He caused so much trouble for days, keep trying to persuade us that the murder is real when it's simply impossible!" continued Pierce. "There are no reports of anyone missing or any witnesses! This is just adding more work for us!"
Benedict lowered his head as Pierce continued complaining.
No matter how hard he tried, no one believed him.
He clenched his fists. He wanted to fight back, but words were stuck in his throat.
He glanced at Alice. She was arranging the papers scattered on the counter while Pierce was continuing his ramble.
What is she up to? He wondered
"Hey, Rosebloom, are you listening?" barked Pierce.
Suddenly, Alice lifted up the pile of papers and swung them towards Pierce. The papers hit his face lightly with a soft whack.
The whole place went silent, shocked at what happened in front of their eyes. Pierce is a strict person; if anyone did that, they would've been dead.
Pierce stayed silent for a few seconds and suddenly snapped, "What was that for?!" He snatched the papers out of Alice's hands.
"You were being annoying," stated Alice.
"I was just telling you-" yelled Pierce.
"It's my choice to believe Mr. Springwood or not." Alice cut off his sentence. Her eyes are filled with determination.
Pierce fell silent.
"Now, will you please help us?" Alice requested.
"You need a better reason for me to let you." Pierce crossed his arms and raised his eyebrows.
"You owe me," said Alice with a smile.
"....Fine." Pierce looked defeated. "Follow me."
"Yay! Thank you, Pierce!" Alice cheered.
Benedict was still processing what was happening. This was the first time he saw Detective Pierce being pulled around by someone.
"Miss Alice, what do you mean by he owes you?" he whispered to her as they walked behind Pierce.
"I saved him countless times! Although he looks smart, he's pretty stupid when it comes to saving himself," said Alice proudly while raising her voice.
"I can hear you, Rosebloom!" Pierce turned around and yelled.

3.title: Chapter 3: What the Warehouse Knew
content: The warehouse door gave easier than it should have for something boarded up for sixty years.
Inside, dust hung in the flashlight beam like it had never once been disturbed, and yet the floor near the far wall was swept clean — recently, deliberately.
Rose followed the clean path to a steel door with no handle, only a rose etched at eye level, its thorns worn smooth by years of fingers tracing the same shape.
She pressed her palm against it without thinking. The door didn't open. But somewhere behind it, something clicked, like a lock recognizing a key it hadn't seen in decades.
"Whoever you are," a voice said from the dark behind her, calm and unhurried, "you have your grandmother's habit of touching things you shouldn't."

Rose spun, flashlight up, hand on her holster. A man stood in the doorway she'd come through, not blocking it, not threatening — just watching, like he'd been waiting for this exact moment for a very long time.
"Who are you?" she asked.
"Someone who's been keeping this door closed for longer than you've been alive," he said. "The question, Detective Auberon, is whether you're ready for what happens when it finally opens."

images.caption: The rose-etched door at the back of the harbor warehouse.
